NASB.1: Then David said, 'This is the house of the LORD God, and this is the altar of burnt offering for Israel.'
NASB.2: So David gave orders to gather the foreigners who were in the land of Israel, and he set stonecutters to hew out stones to build the house of God.
NASB.3: David prepared large quantities of iron to make the nails for the doors of the gates and for the clamps, and more bronze than could be weighed;
NASB.4: and timbers of cedar logs beyond number, for the Sidonians and Tyrians brought large quantities of cedar timber to David.
NASB.5: David said, 'My son Solomon is young and inexperienced, and the house that is to be built for the LORD shall be exceedingly magnificent, famous and glorious throughout all lands. [Therefore] now I will make preparation for it.' So David made ample preparations before his death.
NASB.6: Then he called for his son Solomon, and charged him to build a house for the LORD God of Israel.
NASB.7: David said to Solomon, 'My son, I had intended to build a house to the name of the LORD my God.
NASB.8: 'But the word of the LORD came to me, saying, 'You have shed much blood and have waged great wars; you shall not build a house to My name, because you have shed [so] much blood on the earth before Me.
NASB.9: 'Behold, a son will be born to you, who shall be a man of rest; and I will give him rest from all his enemies on every side; for his name shall be Solomon, and I will give peace and quiet to Israel in his days.
NASB.10: 'He shall build a house for My name, and he shall be My son and I will be his father; and I will establish the throne of his kingdom over Israel forever.'
NASB.11: 'Now, my son, the LORD be with you that you may be successful, and build the house of the LORD your God just as He has spoken concerning you.
NASB.12: 'Only the LORD give you discretion and understanding, and give you charge over Israel, so that you may keep the law of the LORD your God.
NASB.13: 'Then you will prosper, if you are careful to observe the statutes and the ordinances which the LORD commanded Moses concerning Israel. Be strong and courageous, do not fear nor be dismayed.
NASB.14: 'Now behold, with great pains I have prepared for the house of the LORD 100,000 talents of gold and 1,000,000 talents of silver, and bronze and iron beyond weight, for they are in great quantity; also timber and stone I have prepared, and you may add to them.
NASB.15: 'Moreover, there are many workmen with you, stonecutters and masons of stone and carpenters, and all men who are skillful in every kind of work.
NASB.16: 'Of the gold, the silver and the bronze and the iron there is no limit. Arise and work, and may the LORD be with you.'
NASB.17: David also commanded all the leaders of Israel to help his son Solomon, [saying],
NASB.18: 'Is not the LORD your God with you? And has He not given you rest on every side? For He has given the inhabitants of the land into my hand, and the land is subdued before the LORD and before His people.
NASB.19: 'Now set your heart and your soul to seek the LORD your God; arise, therefore, and build the sanctuary of the LORD God, so that you may bring the ark of the covenant of the LORD and the holy vessels of God into the house that is to be built for the name of the LORD.'

NKJV.1: Then David said, “This is the house of the LORD God, and this is the altar of burnt offering for Israel.”
NKJV.2: So David commanded to gather the aliens who were in the land of Israel; and he appointed masons to cut hewn stones to build the house of God.
NKJV.3: And David prepared iron in abundance for the nails of the doors of the gates and for the joints, and bronze in abundance beyond measure,
NKJV.4: and cedar trees in abundance; for the Sidonians and those from Tyre brought much cedar wood to David.
NKJV.5: Now David said, “Solomon my son is young and inexperienced, and the house to be built for the LORD must be exceedingly magnificent, famous and glorious throughout all countries. I will now make preparation for it.” So David made abundant preparations before his death.
NKJV.6: Then he called for his son Solomon, and charged him to build a house for the LORD God of Israel.
NKJV.7: And David said to Solomon: “My son, as for me, it was in my mind to build a house to the name of the LORD my God;
NKJV.8: but the word of the LORD came to me, saying, ‘You have shed much blood and have made great wars; you shall not build a house for My name, because you have shed much blood on the earth in My sight.
NKJV.9: Behold, a son shall be born to you, who shall be a man of rest; and I will give him rest from all his enemies all around. His name shall be Solomon, for I will give peace and quietness to Israel in his days.
NKJV.10: He shall build a house for My name, and he shall be My son, and I will be his Father; and I will establish the throne of his kingdom over Israel forever.’
NKJV.11: Now, my son, may the LORD be with you; and may you prosper, and build the house of the LORD your God, as He has said to you.
NKJV.12: Only may the LORD give you wisdom and understanding, and give you charge concerning Israel, that you may keep the law of the LORD your God.
NKJV.13: Then you will prosper, if you take care to fulfill the statutes and judgments with which the LORD charged Moses concerning Israel. Be strong and of good courage; do not fear nor be dismayed.
NKJV.14: Indeed I have taken much trouble to prepare for the house of the LORD one hundred thousand talents of gold and one million talents of silver, and bronze and iron beyond measure, for it is so abundant. I have prepared timber and stone also, and you may add to them.
NKJV.15: Moreover there are workmen with you in abundance: woodsmen and stonecutters, and all types of skillful men for every kind of work.
NKJV.16: Of gold and silver and bronze and iron there is no limit. Arise and begin working, and the LORD be with you.”
NKJV.17: David also commanded all the leaders of Israel to help Solomon his son, saying,
NKJV.18: “Is not the LORD your God with you? And has He not given you rest on every side? For He has given the inhabitants of the land into my hand, and the land is subdued before the LORD and before His people.
NKJV.19: Now set your heart and your soul to seek the LORD your God. Therefore arise and build the sanctuary of the LORD God, to bring the ark of the covenant of the LORD and the holy articles of God into the house that is to be built for the name of the LORD.”

ESV.1: Then David said, “Here shall be the house of the LORD God and here the altar of burnt offering for Israel.”
ESV.2: David commanded to gather together the resident aliens who were in the land of Israel, and he set stonecutters to prepare dressed stones for building the house of God.
ESV.3: David also provided great quantities of iron for nails for the doors of the gates and for clamps, as well as bronze in quantities beyond weighing,
ESV.4: and cedar timbers without number, for the Sidonians and Tyrians brought great quantities of cedar to David.
ESV.5: For David said, “Solomon my son is young and inexperienced, and the house that is to be built for the LORD must be exceedingly magnificent, of fame and glory throughout all lands. I will therefore make preparation for it.” So David provided materials in great quantity before his death.
ESV.6: Then he called for Solomon his son and charged him to build a house for the LORD, the God of Israel.
ESV.7: David said to Solomon, “My son, I had it in my heart to build a house to the name of the LORD my God.
ESV.8: But the word of the LORD came to me, saying, ‘You have shed much blood and have waged great wars. You shall not build a house to my name, because you have shed so much blood before me on the earth.
ESV.9: Behold, a son shall be born to you who shall be a man of rest. I will give him rest from all his surrounding enemies. For his name shall be Solomon, and I will give peace and quiet to Israel in his days.
ESV.10: He shall build a house for my name. He shall be my son, and I will be his father, and I will establish his royal throne in Israel forever.’
ESV.11: “Now, my son, the LORD be with you, so that you may succeed in building the house of the LORD your God, as he has spoken concerning you.
ESV.12: Only, may the LORD grant you discretion and understanding, that when he gives you charge over Israel you may keep the law of the LORD your God.
ESV.13: Then you will prosper if you are careful to observe the statutes and the rules that the LORD commanded Moses for Israel. Be strong and courageous. Fear not; do not be dismayed.
ESV.14: With great pains I have provided for the house of the LORD 100,000 talents  of gold, a million talents of silver, and bronze and iron beyond weighing, for there is so much of it; timber and stone, too, I have provided. To these you must add.
ESV.15: You have an abundance of workmen: stonecutters, masons, carpenters, and all kinds of craftsmen without number, skilled in working
ESV.16: gold, silver, bronze, and iron. Arise and work! The LORD be with you!”
ESV.17: David also commanded all the leaders of Israel to help Solomon his son, saying,
ESV.18: “Is not the LORD your God with you? And has he not given you peace  on every side? For he has delivered the inhabitants of the land into my hand, and the land is subdued before the LORD and his people.
ESV.19: Now set your mind and heart to seek the LORD your God. Arise and build the sanctuary of the LORD God, so that the ark of the covenant of the LORD and the holy vessels of God may be brought into a house built for the name of the LORD.”

CSB17.1: Then David said, “This is the house of the LORD God, and this is the altar of burnt offering for Israel.” <sup>ⓝ</sup>
CSB17.2: So David gave orders to gather the resident aliens that were in the land of Israel, <sup>ⓐ</sup> and he appointed stonecutters to cut finished stones for building God’s house. <sup>ⓑ</sup>
CSB17.3: David supplied a great deal of iron to make the nails for the doors of the gates and for the fittings, together with an immeasurable quantity of bronze, <sup>ⓒ</sup>
CSB17.4: and innumerable cedar logs because the Sidonians and Tyrians had brought a large quantity of cedar logs to David. <sup>ⓓ</sup>
CSB17.5: David said, “My son Solomon is young and inexperienced, and the house that is to be built for the LORD must be exceedingly great and famous and glorious in all the lands. <sup>ⓔ</sup> Therefore, I will make provision for it.” So David made lavish preparations for it before his death.
CSB17.6: Then he summoned his son Solomon and charged him to build a house for the LORD God of Israel.
CSB17.7: “My son,” David said to Solomon, “It was in my heart to build a house for the name of the LORD my God, <sup>ⓕ</sup>
CSB17.8: but the word of the LORD came to me: ‘You have shed much blood and waged great wars. You are not to build a house for my name because you have shed so much blood on the ground before me. <sup>ⓖ</sup>
CSB17.9: But a son will be born to you; he will be a man of rest. I will give him rest from all his surrounding enemies, <sup>ⓗ</sup> for his name will be Solomon, <sup>[1]</sup> <sup>ⓘ</sup> and I will give peace and quiet to Israel during his reign. <sup>ⓙ</sup>
CSB17.10: He is the one who will build a house for my name. He will be my son, and I will be his father. I will establish the throne of his kingdom over Israel forever.’ <sup>ⓚ</sup>
CSB17.11: “Now, my son, may the LORD be with you, <sup>ⓛ</sup> and may you succeed in building the house of the LORD your God, as he said about you.
CSB17.12: Above all, may the LORD give you insight and understanding when he puts you in charge of Israel so that you may keep the law of the LORD your God. <sup>ⓜ</sup>
CSB17.13: Then you will succeed if you carefully follow the statutes and ordinances the LORD commanded Moses for Israel. <sup>ⓝ</sup> Be strong and courageous. Don’t be afraid or discouraged. <sup>ⓐ</sup>
CSB17.14: “Notice I have taken great pains to provide for the house of the LORD  — 3,775 tons of gold, 37,750 tons of silver, <sup>[2]</sup> <sup>ⓑ</sup> and bronze and iron that can’t be weighed because there is so much of it. I have also provided timber and stone, but you will need to add more to them.
CSB17.15: You also have many workers: stonecutters, masons, carpenters, and people skilled in every kind of work
CSB17.16: in gold, silver, bronze, and iron — beyond number. Now begin the work, and may the LORD be with you.” <sup>ⓒ</sup>
CSB17.17: Then David ordered all the leaders of Israel to help his son Solomon:
CSB17.18: “The LORD your God is with you, isn’t he? And hasn’t he given you rest on every side? <sup>ⓓ</sup> For he has handed the land’s inhabitants over to me, and the land has been subdued before the LORD and his people.
CSB17.19: Now determine in your mind and heart to seek the LORD your God. <sup>ⓔ</sup> Get started building the LORD God’s sanctuary so that you may bring the ark of the LORD’s covenant and the holy articles of God to the temple that is to be built <sup>ⓕ</sup> for the name of the LORD.” <sup>ⓖ</sup>

NLT.1: Then David said, “This will be the location for the Temple of the LORD God and the place of the altar for Israel’s burnt offerings!”
NLT.2: So David gave orders to call together the foreigners living in Israel, and he assigned them the task of preparing finished stone for building the Temple of God.
NLT.3: David provided large amounts of iron for the nails that would be needed for the doors in the gates and for the clamps, and he gave more bronze than could be weighed.
NLT.4: He also provided innumerable cedar logs, for the men of Tyre and Sidon had brought vast amounts of cedar to David.
NLT.5: David said, “My son Solomon is still young and inexperienced. And since the Temple to be built for the LORD must be a magnificent structure, famous and glorious throughout the world, I will begin making preparations for it now.” So David collected vast amounts of building materials before his death.
NLT.6: Then David sent for his son Solomon and instructed him to build a Temple for the LORD, the God of Israel.
NLT.7: “My son, I wanted to build a Temple to honor the name of the LORD my God,” David told him.
NLT.8: “But the LORD said to me, ‘You have killed many men in the battles you have fought. And since you have shed so much blood in my sight, you will not be the one to build a Temple to honor my name.
NLT.9: But you will have a son who will be a man of peace. I will give him peace with his enemies in all the surrounding lands. His name will be Solomon, and I will give peace and quiet to Israel during his reign.
NLT.10: He is the one who will build a Temple to honor my name. He will be my son, and I will be his father. And I will secure the throne of his kingdom over Israel forever.’
NLT.11: “Now, my son, may the LORD be with you and give you success as you follow his directions in building the Temple of the LORD your God.
NLT.12: And may the LORD give you wisdom and understanding, that you may obey the Law of the LORD your God as you rule over Israel.
NLT.13: For you will be successful if you carefully obey the decrees and regulations that the LORD gave to Israel through Moses. Be strong and courageous; do not be afraid or lose heart!
NLT.14: “I have worked hard to provide materials for building the Temple of the LORD — nearly 4,000 tons of gold, 40,000 tons of silver, and so much iron and bronze that it cannot be weighed. I have also gathered timber and stone for the walls, though you may need to add more.
NLT.15: You have a large number of skilled stonemasons and carpenters and craftsmen of every kind.
NLT.16: You have expert goldsmiths and silversmiths and workers of bronze and iron. Now begin the work, and may the LORD be with you!”
NLT.17: Then David ordered all the leaders of Israel to assist Solomon in this project.
NLT.18: “The LORD your God is with you,” he declared. “He has given you peace with the surrounding nations. He has handed them over to me, and they are now subject to the LORD and his people.
NLT.19: Now seek the LORD your God with all your heart and soul. Build the sanctuary of the LORD God so that you can bring the Ark of the LORD’s Covenant and the holy vessels of God into the Temple built to honor the LORD’s name.”

WEB.1: Then David said, “This is the house of Yahweh God, and this is the altar of burnt offering for Israel.”
WEB.2: David gave orders to gather together the foreigners who were in the land of Israel; and he set masons to cut dressed stones to build God’s house.
WEB.3: David prepared iron in abundance for the nails for the doors of the gates, and for the couplings; and brass in abundance without weight;
WEB.4: and cedar trees without number, for the Sidonians and the people of Tyre brought cedar trees in abundance to David.
WEB.5: David said, “Solomon my son is young and tender, and the house that is to be built for Yahweh must be exceedingly magnificent, of fame and of glory throughout all countries. I will therefore make preparation for it.” So David prepared abundantly before his death.
WEB.6: Then he called for Solomon his son, and commanded him to build a house for Yahweh, the God of Israel.
WEB.7: David said to Solomon his son, “As for me, it was in my heart to build a house to the name of Yahweh my God.
WEB.8: But Yahweh’s word came to me, saying, ‘You have shed blood abundantly, and have made great wars. You shall not build a house to my name, because you have shed much blood on the earth in my sight.
WEB.9: Behold, a son shall be born to you, who shall be a man of peace. I will give him rest from all his enemies all around; for his name shall be Solomon, and I will give peace and quietness to Israel in his days.
WEB.10: He shall build a house for my name; and he will be my son, and I will be his father; and I will establish the throne of his kingdom over Israel for ever.’
WEB.11: Now, my son, may Yahweh be with you and prosper you, and build the house of Yahweh your God, as he has spoken concerning you.
WEB.12: May Yahweh give you discretion and understanding, and put you in charge of Israel; that so you may keep the law of Yahweh your God.
WEB.13: Then you will prosper, if you observe to do the statutes and the ordinances which Yahweh gave Moses concerning Israel. Be strong and courageous. Don’t be afraid, and don’t be dismayed.
WEB.14: Now, behold, in my affliction I have prepared for Yahweh’s house one hundred thousand talents  of gold, one million talents  of silver, and brass and iron without weight; for it is in abundance. I have also prepared timber and stone; and you may add to them.
WEB.15: There are also workmen with you in abundance, cutters and workers of stone and timber, and all kinds of men who are skillful in every kind of work;
WEB.16: of the gold, the silver, the brass, and the iron, there is no number. Arise and be doing, and may Yahweh be with you.”
WEB.17: David also commanded all the princes of Israel to help Solomon his son, saying,
WEB.18: “Isn’t Yahweh your God with you? Hasn’t he given you rest on every side? For he has delivered the inhabitants of the land into my hand; and the land is subdued before Yahweh, and before his people.
WEB.19: Now set your heart and your soul to follow Yahweh your God. Arise therefore, and build the sanctuary of Yahweh God, to bring the ark of Yahweh’s covenant and the holy vessels of God into the house that is to be built for Yahweh’s name.”

AMP.6: Then he called for Solomon his son and ordered him to build a house for the LORD, the God of Israel.
AMP.7: David said to Solomon, "My son, I had intended to build a house for the Name (Presence) of the LORD my God.
AMP.8: But the word of the LORD came to me, saying, 'You have shed much blood and have waged great wars; you shall not build a house for My Name, because you have shed so much blood on the earth before me.
AMP.9: Behold, a son will be born to you, who will be a man of peace. I will give him rest from all his enemies on every side; for his name shall be Solomon, and I will give peace and quiet to Israel in his days.
AMP.10: He shall build a house for My Name (Presence). He shall be My son and I will be his father; and I will establish his royal throne over Israel forever.'
AMP.11: Now, my son, may the LORD be with you so that you may be successful and build the house of the LORD your God, just as He has spoken concerning you.
AMP.12: Only may the LORD give you wisdom and understanding, and give you charge over Israel, so that you may keep the law of the LORD your God.
AMP.13: Then you will prosper, if you are careful to observe and fulfill the statutes and ordinances which the LORD commanded Moses concerning Israel. Be strong and courageous, do not fear nor be dismayed.
AMP.14: Now listen, with great trouble I have prepared and provided for the house of the LORD 100,000 talents of gold, 1,000,000 talents of silver, and bronze and iron beyond weighing, for they are great in quantity. I have also prepared and provided timber and stone, and you may add to them.
AMP.15: Further, you have workmen in abundance: stonecutters and stonemasons and carpenters, and all men who are skillful in every kind of work.
AMP.16: As for the gold, the silver, the bronze, and the iron, there is no limit. So arise and begin working, and may the LORD be with you."
AMP.17: David also commanded all the leaders of Israel to help Solomon his son, saying,
AMP.18: "Is not the LORD your God with you? And has He not given you rest and peace on every side? For He has given the inhabitants of the land into my hand, and the land is subdued before the LORD and before His people.
AMP.19: Now set your heart and your soul to seek (inquire of, require as your vital necessity) the LORD your God. Arise and build the sanctuary of the LORD God, so that you may bring the ark of the covenant of the LORD and the holy articles and utensils of God into the house built for the Name (Presence) of the LORD."

MSG.1: So David declared, "From now on, this is the site for the worship of God; this is the place for Israel's Altar of Burnt Offering."
MSG.2: David ordered all the resident aliens in the land to come together; he sent them to the stone quarries to cut dressed stone to build The Temple of God.
MSG.3: He also stockpiled a huge quantity of iron for nails and bracings for the doors of the gates, more bronze than could be weighed,
MSG.4: and cedar logs past counting (the Sidonians and Tyrians shipped in huge loads of cedar logs for David).
MSG.5: David was thinking, "My son Solomon is too young to plan ahead for this. But the sanctuary that is to be built for God has to be the greatest, the talk of all the nations; so I'll get the construction materials together." That's why David prepared this huge stockpile of building materials before he died.
MSG.6: Then he called in Solomon his son and commanded him to build a sanctuary for the God of Israel.
MSG.7: David said to Solomon, "I wanted in the worst way to build a sanctuary to honor my God.
MSG.8: But God prevented me, saying, 'You've killed too many people, fought too many wars. You are not the one to honor me by building a sanctuary—you've been responsible for too much killing, too much bloodshed.
MSG.9: But you are going to have a son and he will be a quiet and peaceful man, and I will calm his enemies down on all sides. His very name will speak peace—that is, Solomon, which means Peace—and I'll give peace and rest under his rule.
MSG.10: He will be the one to build a sanctuary in my honor. He'll be my royal adopted son and I'll be his father; and I'll make sure that the authority of his kingdom over Israel lasts forever.'
MSG.11: "So now, son, God be with you. God-speed as you build the sanctuary for your God, the job God has given you.
MSG.12: And may God also give you discernment and understanding when he puts you in charge of Israel so that you will rule in reverent obedience under God's Revelation.
MSG.13: That's what will make you successful, following the directions and doing the things that God commanded Moses for Israel. Courage! Take charge! Don't be timid; don't hold back.
MSG.14: Look at this—I've gone to a lot of trouble to stockpile materials for the sanctuary of God: 100,000 talents (3,775 tons) of gold, a million talents (37,750 tons) of silver, tons of bronze and iron—too much to weigh—and all this timber and stone. And you're free to add more.
MSG.15: And workers both plentiful and prepared: stonecutters, masons, carpenters, artisans in
MSG.16: gold and silver, bronze and iron. You're all set—get to work! And God-speed!"
MSG.17: David gave orders to all of Israel's leaders to help his son Solomon,
MSG.18: saying, "Isn't it obvious that your God is present with you; that he has given you peaceful relations with everyone around? My part in this was to put down the enemies, subdue the land to God and his people;
MSG.19: your part is to give yourselves, heart and soul, to praying to your God. So get moving—build the sacred house of worship to God! Then bring the Chest of the Covenant of God and all the holy furnishings for the worship of God into the sanctuary built in honor of God."

NIV.1: Then David said, “The house of the Lord God is to be here, and also the altar of burnt offering for Israel.”
NIV.2:
Preparations for the Temple
So David gave orders to assemble the aliens living in Israel, and from among them he appointed stonecutters to prepare dressed stone for building the house of God.
NIV.3: He provided a large amount of iron to make nails for the doors of the gateways and for the fittings, and more bronze than could be weighed.
NIV.4: He also provided more cedar logs than could be counted, for the Sidonians and Tyrians had brought large numbers of them to David.
NIV.5: David said, “My son Solomon is young and inexperienced, and the house to be built for the Lord should be of great magnificence and fame and splendor in the sight of all the nations. Therefore I will make preparations for it.” So David made extensive preparations before his death.
NIV.6: Then he called for his son Solomon and charged him to build a house for the Lord, the God of Israel.
NIV.7: David said to Solomon: “My son, I had it in my heart to build a house for the Name of the Lord my God.
NIV.8: But this word of the Lord came to me: ‘You have shed much blood and have fought many wars. You are not to build a house for my Name, because you have shed much blood on the earth in my sight.
NIV.9: But you will have a son who will be a man of peace and rest, and I will give him rest from all his enemies on every side. His name will be Solomon, and I will grant Israel peace and quiet during his reign.
NIV.10: He is the one who will build a house for my Name. He will be my son, and I will be his father. And I will establish the throne of his kingdom over Israel forever.’
NIV.11: “Now, my son, the Lord be with you, and may you have success and build the house of the Lord your God, as he said you would.
NIV.12: May the Lord give you discretion and understanding when he puts you in command over Israel, so that you may keep the law of the Lord your God.
NIV.13: Then you will have success if you are careful to observe the decrees and laws that the Lord gave Moses for Israel. Be strong and courageous. Do not be afraid or discouraged.
NIV.14: “I have taken great pains to provide for the temple of the Lord a hundred thousand talents of gold, a million talents of silver, quantities of bronze and iron too great to be weighed, and wood and stone. And you may add to them.
NIV.15: You have many workmen: stonecutters, masons and carpenters, as well as men skilled in every kind of work
NIV.16: in gold and silver, bronze and iron—craftsmen beyond number. Now begin the work, and the Lord be with you.”
NIV.17: Then David ordered all the leaders of Israel to help his son Solomon.
NIV.18: He said to them, “Is not the Lord your God with you? And has he not granted you rest on every side? For he has handed the inhabitants of the land over to me, and the land is subject to the Lord and to his people.
NIV.19: Now devote your heart and soul to seeking the Lord your God. Begin to build the sanctuary of the Lord God, so that you may bring the ark of the covenant of the Lord and the sacred articles belonging to God into the temple that will be built for the Name of the Lord.”

NET.1: David then said, “This is the place where the temple of the LORD God will be, along with the altar for burnt sacrifices for Israel.”
NET.2: David ordered the resident foreigners in the land of Israel to be called together. He appointed some of them to be stonecutters to chisel stones for the building of God’s temple.
NET.3: David supplied a large amount of iron for the nails of the doors of the gates and for braces, more bronze than could be weighed,
NET.4: and more cedar logs than could be counted. (The Sidonians and Tyrians had brought a large amount of cedar logs to David.)
NET.5: David said, “My son Solomon is just an inexperienced young man, and the temple to be built for the LORD must be especially magnificent so it will become famous and be considered splendid by all the nations. Therefore I will make preparations for its construction.” So David made extensive preparations before he died.
NET.6: He summoned his son Solomon and charged him to build a temple for the LORD God of Israel.
NET.7: David said to Solomon: “My son, I really wanted to build a temple to honor the LORD my God.
NET.8: But the LORD said to me: ‘You have spilled a great deal of blood and fought many battles. You must not build a temple to honor me, for you have spilled a great deal of blood on the ground before me.
NET.9: Look, you will have a son, who will be a peaceful man. I will give him rest from all his enemies on every side. Indeed, Solomon will be his name; I will give Israel peace and quiet during his reign.
NET.10: He will build a temple to honor me; he will become my son, and I will become his father. I will grant to his dynasty permanent rule over Israel.’
NET.11: “Now, my son, may the LORD be with you! May you succeed and build a temple for the LORD your God, just as he announced you would.
NET.12: Only may the LORD give you insight and understanding when he places you in charge of Israel, so you may obey the law of the LORD your God.
NET.13: Then you will succeed, if you carefully obey the rules and regulations which the LORD ordered Moses to give to Israel. Be strong and brave! Don’t be afraid and don’t panic!
NET.14: Now, look, I have made every effort to supply what is needed to build the LORD’s temple. I have stored up 100,000 talents of gold, 1,000,000 talents of silver, and so much bronze and iron it cannot be weighed, as well as wood and stones. Feel free to add more!
NET.15: You also have available many workers, including stonecutters, masons, carpenters, and an innumerable array of workers who are skilled
NET.16: in using gold, silver, bronze, and iron. Get up and begin the work! May the LORD be with you!”
NET.17: David ordered all the officials of Israel to support his son Solomon.
NET.18: He told them, “The LORD your God is with you! He has made you secure on every side, for he handed over to me the inhabitants of the region and the region is subdued before the LORD and his people.
NET.19: Now seek the LORD your God wholeheartedly and with your entire being! Get up and build the sanctuary of the LORD God! Then you can bring the ark of the LORD’s covenant and the holy items dedicated to God’s service into the temple that is built to honor the LORD.”
